121: Notebook lifecycle configurations automate environment setup at creation or startup.
Installing a separate Systems Manager agent is unnecessary and assumes direct management of the underlying service-owned instance.
An .ipynb file is not an operating-system startup script simply because it is placed under /etc/init.
A manual conda installation does not provide the requested automatic setup when the notebook is created or restarted.
Attach a lifecycle configuration that installs the required packages into the intended environment at the appropriate lifecycle stage.
122: Entity matching identifies records representing the same entity even when some identifying fields differ.
Athena does not provide the asserted built-in FindDuplicates query as a ready-made entity-matching service.
Glue FindMatches learns record-matching behavior from examples, helping link new accounts to records of known fraudulent users.
A crawler discovers schema and partitions; it does not infer which accounts belong to the same person.
The Data Catalog stores metadata, not a trained matching model that detects duplicate identities in application records.
123: With rare fraud, overall accuracy can conceal many false negatives; weighting and suitable model selection focus attention on positive examples.
RMSE is not the most informative fraud classification evaluation metric and does not directly emphasize missed fraud.
Increasing scale_pos_weight makes positive examples more influential in XGBoost's loss, helping the model detect the rare fraudulent class.
The confusion matrix does not establish underfitting or prove that deeper trees are needed; extra depth can overfit.
Use AUC to evaluate/select models by discrimination rather than majority-class accuracy. Changing eval_metric alone does not alter the training loss or guarantee fewer false negatives.
The stated evidence does not establish overfitting, so decreasing depth is not the direct class-imbalance remedy offered by B and D.
124: Attention lets a sequence decoder access relevant encoder states instead of relying on a single compressed representation.
Changing to n-grams does not directly resolve the encoder–decoder difficulty of retaining information over long sentences.
Hidden-unit count does not need to exceed sentence word count; this rule does not fix long-range alignment.
Tuning the attention configuration improves how the decoder uses source positions, directly addressing degradation on longer sentences.
Initialization can affect training, but it does not specifically address the long-input information bottleneck described.
125: For a rare positive class, evaluate how many positives are recovered and how reliable positive predictions remain.
Specificity measures correctly rejected legitimate transactions, not the fraction of fraud cases captured.
False-positive rate measures false alarms among negatives, rather than positive-case coverage.
A model predicting every transaction as legitimate would already achieve about 98% accuracy while detecting no fraud.
PR-AUC summarizes the precision–recall trade-off and is informative when fraudulent examples are rare.
True-positive rate is recall: the fraction of actual fraudulent transactions detected by the classifier.
126: Container network isolation prevents training code from making network calls that could exfiltrate accessible data.
Removing S3 permissions may prevent required input/output operations, but does not itself stop every outbound network path from malicious code.
Encrypting model weights does not block a training process from sending the plaintext data it can access to another host.
At-rest encryption does not stop exfiltration by a process that legitimately receives decrypted training data.
Network isolation blocks container network access; SageMaker manages the permitted training input/output transfer outside that isolated container.
127: A private labeling workforce controls who sees the scans, while localization labels identify regions within images.
A custom labeling tool and queue require development and operations that Ground Truth already provides.
A public Mechanical Turk workforce conflicts with the authorized-only requirement, and image classification does not mark regions of concern.
Ground Truth's private workforce restricts labeling access, and the bounding-box task supplies localized annotations with managed workflow components.
Building authentication, a web app, and workflow backend requires substantially more effort than a built-in private Ground Truth labeling job.
128: Human review should target uncertain extraction results before those errors propagate into downstream validation.
Ground Truth creates labeled training datasets; A2I is the integration designed for human review of Textract inference results.
Switching request mode changes how the operation is called, not the quality of low-confidence extracted fields.
A2I can route selected low-confidence Textract results to human reviewers before business validation. This is a historical service path with restricted new-customer availability.
Rekognition text detection is not a replacement for the document extraction and targeted review workflow needed for these dense scanned documents.
129: Provisioned Kinesis shard count limits aggregate stream throughput and can become the bottleneck before delivery.
More S3 prefixes do not increase the upstream stream's shard throughput, which is the first capacity issue to investigate here.
Shorter retention removes the opportunity to replay older data but does not increase write or consumer throughput.
Additional shards increase aggregate stream capacity when traffic is distributed appropriately. Verify shard and Firehose metrics to confirm the actual bottleneck.
Extra consumers do not increase producer write capacity and can compete for shared read throughput.
130: A test set for new-customer recommendations should contain users entirely absent from training.
Random interaction splitting can place the same customer's history in both sets, making evaluation easier than the intended new-user scenario.
Holding out recent interactions tests future behavior for already known users, not generalization to wholly new users.
Selecting only users with few interactions biases the test population rather than taking a representative sample of new users.
Hold out every interaction for a random user subset, so evaluation measures generalization to unseen customers using their available preference features.
131: Controlling access paths and isolating container networking reduces opportunities to move confidential data outside the intended environment.
PrivateLink supplies a private API path that can be constrained with endpoint and IAM policies; it must be combined with restrictions on alternate egress paths.
SCPs set permission boundaries but a general restriction on SageMaker access does not specifically implement the required notebook/container egress controls.
Disabling root limits system administration but does not prevent ordinary user code from sending data through permitted network connections.
Network isolation prevents training and inference containers from making network calls, directly restricting their ability to exfiltrate data.
Restricting notebook presigned-URL use to corporate source IPs reduces unauthorized remote access to the notebook and its data.
Encryption protects confidentiality on storage and transport, but an authorized process can still transmit decrypted data unless access and egress are controlled.
132: Managed discovery, ETL, SQL, and visualization services minimize custom infrastructure for an evolving data lake.
EMR can perform the processing, but generally requires more cluster/application configuration than Glue's managed discovery and ETL workflow.
Streaming analytics does not replace schema discovery, and combining EMR with a warehouse adds management beyond the stated needs.
Glue discovers and transforms data, Athena queries the S3 results, and QuickSight supplies dashboards with little infrastructure to manage.
Custom Lambda discovery/transformation chains and orchestration add code for capabilities already provided by Glue.
133: OCR extracts text; entity recognition identifies meaningful spans and domain-specific labels within that text.
BlazingText supports word embeddings and text classification, not the proposed turnkey named-entity extraction workflow.
A marketplace OCR model and custom NER model require selection, hosting, and retraining work compared with managed document/NLP services.
Textract supplies managed OCR, while Comprehend's standard and custom entity recognition address general and receipt-specific entities with less custom infrastructure.
Replacing managed Textract with a separately selected OCR model adds integration and operation work without a stated need.
134: The caller's permission to create a job is separate from the execution role used by that job to access resources.
Permissions attached only to the notebook role are not automatically inherited by a Processing job unless that role is explicitly supplied as its execution role.
The notebook caller creates the job and passes an execution role; that role supplies S3, KMS, and ECR access. The caller also needs iam:PassRole.
VPC endpoints provide connectivity, not the missing execution-role authorizations to read, decrypt, and write data.
Long-lived user keys are not the Processing execution-role mechanism and unnecessarily expose credentials; the proposed permissions also omit required S3 access.
135: Managed notebook updates are applied through the SageMaker notebook instance lifecycle.
Creating a lifecycle configuration creates a setup script resource; it does not itself update the running managed system software.
The service-owned notebook volume is not a customer-managed EBS volume that can simply be detached and mounted onto a new notebook.
Stopping and starting the notebook allows SageMaker to apply the service-provided updated environment while retaining the persistent notebook storage.
Editing lifecycle script configuration does not itself refresh the managed notebook's base software image.
136: Storage encryption, encrypted API transport, and AI-service data-use preferences are distinct controls.
Historically, S3 server-side encryption, HTTPS API use, and the Support opt-out process addressed the requirements. Current opt-out management uses AWS Organizations AI services policies.
A Rekognition collection stores face representations rather than the original image archive and does not replace storage encryption or data-use opt-out controls.
Moving Regions and adding a VPN do not by themselves establish the required storage encryption and service-improvement opt-out settings.
Client-encrypted image objects are not directly usable as ordinary Rekognition S3 image input, and a VPN does not set the service-improvement opt-out policy.
137: Edge inference processes video locally and sends only compact events, reducing bandwidth use.
Streaming every camera feed to AWS conflicts with the stated bandwidth constraint.
Rekognition is a managed cloud API, not a model that can simply be enabled locally on a DeepLens camera as described.
Calling a cloud SageMaker endpoint still requires image transfers from each location and does not provide the proposed local-video processing advantage.
In the historical solution, the deployed model and local Lambda count people on the cameras and send alerts. DeepLens is retired; the underlying edge-inference principle remains applicable.
138: A scale-out cooldown allows newly added capacity time to become effective before further scaling decisions.
Scale-in timing controls removals, not the premature additions described, and raising maximum capacity does not fix the timing.
A multi-model endpoint addresses model consolidation, not the cooldown behavior of additional instances.
An API Gateway/Lambda invocation layer does not change the endpoint autoscaling policy's timing.
Increase the scale-out cooldown to account for provisioning and model startup, reducing repeated additions before new capacity is ready.
139: Add a model as an endpoint production variant before routing requests to it or adjusting its traffic weight.
Create a configuration containing the new zero-weight variant and update the endpoint. Use TargetVariant for preview users, then gradually increase the variant's live traffic weight.
SageMaker's native variant routing avoids a custom ALB architecture, and the asserted direct endpoint/TargetVariant ALB integration is not the intended mechanism.
UpdateEndpointWeightsAndCapacities changes existing variants; it cannot introduce a new model variant that is absent from the endpoint configuration.
Separate endpoints and application/DNS routing add management and do not provide the direct per-request TargetVariant control available on one endpoint.
140: IP Insights learns typical associations between entity identifiers and IP addresses from observed pairs.
Labeling login success does not directly identify whether a user–IP pairing is unusual, and adds an unnecessary supervised labeling step.
IP Insights models user/IP associations without requiring fraud labels; periodic retraining incorporates evolving normal access patterns.
IP Insights is not configured as the described supervised binary classifier, and successful/failed access labels do not define the desired unusual-location target.
Object2Vec is a general embedding algorithm; IP Insights is specifically designed for the user–IP association anomaly use case.
